caption: The drawing depicts an old Spanish lock, primarily rendered in shades of brown and gray to represent the metallic texture of the lock and its components. The main feature is a large, round lock plate with a series of evenly spaced rivets or nails depicted as small white circles around its circumference. Attached to this plate is a sizable, straight handle with a slightly ornate design at its pivoting point, which extends diagonally from the top left to the center of the plate. Below the handle, there is a detailed keyhole and an inserted key with a simple, rectangular bow and a string or cord hanging from it. In the top right corner of the drawing, there is a smaller, inset illustration featuring the same lock handle and a decorative plate, both rendered on a blue-green background. The drawing also includes handwritten text, with the prominent inscription reading "Old Spanish Lock hand wrought in New Mexico." The artist's name and location, "Mable G. Claflin, Taos-New Mexico," are noted in the lower left corner in small text. The overall color palette consists of muted earth tones, with a splash of blue-green in the inset illustration.
title: Spanish Lock
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
